03/14/2025 – 11:15 AM
Sent initial contact letter via email and regular mail. Also texted clmt a link to the claims portal so she can upload her photos. She confirmed reciept of the text but hasnt uploaded yet. Vehicle inspection scheduled for 03/19 at clmt's residence. Wait – this is a water loss, not auto. Typo above, ignore. I meant to write "property inspection." Inspection is set for 03/19 at 10 AM. I will be there with Dave from Apex Restoration, who will be handling the mitigation. Dave said he can meet us on site. I confirmed with clmt that she will be home.

03/19/2025 – 10:00 AM – Property Inspection / Apex On-Site
Met Peterson at the house. Walked the basement with her and Dave. Water line visible on the drywall, about 12-14 inches up in the main family room area. Sump pump pit had water in it but the pump itself was not running when we arrived. Dave checked it – the float switch appears stuck, and there's a visible crack in the discharge pipe near the check valve. Looks like the pump may have run continuously and burned out, or the float just failed. Either way, pump is likely a maintenance item vs. sudden failure – need to review the policy language on this. Took photos of the pump and the pit.

Basement layout: finished family room (carpet, drywall, built-in shelving), a small bathroom (vinyl floor, vanity), and a utility room (unfinished, concrete floor). Water affected the family room and bathroom. Utility room has some dampness on the bottom of the stored boxes but no standing water. Carpet in the family room is saturated – Peterson had already pulled up about a third of it and rolled it against the wall. She also moved a couch and a recliner into the garage. Noted the furniture has water stains on the legs.

Claim #CL-2025-04873 claim status is under review. Record status: current.

Drywall – water line visible, will need to be cut out at least 2 ft above the line. Dave estimated the affected area at about 400 sq ft for the family room. The bathroom vinyl is likely going to need to be pulled up too, the pad underneath is wet. Dave is going to set up air movers and a dehumidifier tomorrow morning. He said he can start demo today if Peterson is ok with it – she said yes, go ahead. I gave her a heads up that the drywall and carpet are likely a total loss.

03/19/2025 – 12:15 PM
Spoke with Peterson about the sump pump. She said she had it serviced about 2 years ago, but she doesn't have the receipt. She thinks the pump was original to the house, so about 15 years old. I explained we'd need to determine if the failure was sudden or due to wear and tear – told her I'd check the policy and get back to her. She was a little frustrated, said "it worked fine until it didn't." I understand her point, but we have to follow the policy. I also asked about the floor drain – she said there is one in the utility room, and it was backing up when she got home. That complicates things – sewer backup is a separate coverage. Need to check if she has that endorsement. She isnt sure. I'll have to look at the policy.

Apex started demo today. Dave called to say they found some wet insulation in the wall cavities and will be removing that as well. Also, the subfloor in the family room is particle board and it's swollen in a couple of areas – he recommends replacing it, but wants me to take a look before he does. I told him I'd swing by tomorrow morning. He also mentioned the bathroom vanity is water damaged – the particle board doors are swollen and won't close right. I'll take a look at that too.

documents.title: Claim Notes – CL-2025-04873 (Peterson)
documents.content:
03/21/2025 – 1:30 PM
Pulled the policy to check on sewer backup coverage. Peterson has a basic HO-3 with no sewer or drain endorsement. That means the backup from the floor drain is not covered. Called her to explain – she was quiet for a moment, then said "so the water that came up through the drain is just my problem?" I told her I understand the frustration and that we can talk about options, but the policy is clear. She asked if the sump pump failure is covered at least. I said I'm still working on that – need to determine if it was a sudden failure or mechanical breakdown. She said the pump was making a grinding noise for a few weeks before it stopped, which she mentioned to me before. That's a red flag for wear and tear. I'll need to look at this more carefully.

03/22/2025 – 10:00 AM
Dave called – the crew found more damage in the wall behind the vanity. The plumbing supply line to the vanity was loose at the shut-off valve and had been leaking slowly for a while, not just during the sump failure. There's water staining on the studs and the drywall was wet all the way up to the top plate. He's going to have to open up more of the wall to dry it out. I told him to go ahead – better to find it now than later. This changes the picture a bit – if the main loss is from the sump failure but there's also a slow leak, we need to document both. The slow leak might be considered a separate occurrence, or it might be excluded if it's long-term. Need to think about this.

03/22/2025 – 2:00 PM
Spoke with my supervisor, Karen, about the claim. I laid out what we have: sump pump failure, water in the family room and bathroom, sewer backup through the floor drain (not covered), and now this slow leak from the vanity supply line. She said the slow leak is probably maintenance – homeowner should have caught it – but she wants me to document it thoroughly and let underwriting know. She also said to get a statement from Peterson about when she last used the vanity or noticed any issues. I'll call her tomorrow.

03/24/2025 – 9:15 AM
Called Peterson to get a statement about the vanity leak. She said she doesn't use that bathroom much – it's the guest bath – and she last went in there maybe two weeks before the flood, and everything seemed fine. She did say the shut-off valve under the sink had a small drip a few months back and her husband (they're divorced) had tightened it with a wrench. She doesn't know if that helped or made it worse. I asked if she had any documentation of that – she said no, it was just something he did when he was over helping with something else. Noted in file.

Claim #CL-2025-04873 claim amount requested is 12500 USD. Record status: current.

03/24/2025 – 3:45 PM
Received the initial repair estimate from Apex. Dave's crew has been documenting everything as they go. The estimate includes:
- Demo and removal of wet drywall, insulation, subfloor (family room), vanity, carpet, and pad
- Drying equipment rental (air movers, dehumidifiers) – 5 days
- New drywall, tape, float, texture – family room and bathroom
- New subfloor – family room (estimated 200 sq ft)
- New vanity and countertop – bathroom
- New carpet and pad – family room (they'll match as close as possible)
- Paint – family room and bathroom
- Reinstall shut-off valve, new supply lines
- Permit fees

The total came to $11,850. I reviewed it line by line – the numbers look reasonable for our area. Labor rates are in line with what we usually pay. I'll need to get this reviewed by Karen before I present it to Peterson.

03/25/2025 – 11:00 AM
Karen reviewed the Apex estimate this morning. She thought the drying time was a little long – Dave estimated 5 days but Karen said with the amount of water, 4 should be enough. She also questioned the carpet allowance – she wants me to check if we should be paying for upgraded pad or just the standard. I told her I'd talk to Dave. She also reminded me that we need to get a signed proof of loss from Peterson before we issue any payment. I'll need to get that done soon.

documents.title: Claim Notes – CL-2025-04873 (Peterson)
documents.content:
03/27/2025 – 9:15 AM
Peterson came in and signed the proof of loss. Went through the Apex estimate with her line by line – she didn't push back on any of the numbers. She asked if the check would be made out to her or to Apex. I explained that we typically issue a two-party check made out to her and the contractor, or we can pay Apex directly and she just covers the deductible. She said she'd need to think about it. She also asked about the shut-off valve – whether the repair/replacement was covered. I told her that if the valve itself failed, that's something we'd need to look at, but if it was a pre-existing leak that wasn't maintained, it might not be covered. She said she understood. She left the photos – I'll scan them in and attach to the claim file.

03/27/2025 – 2:00 PM
Scanned Peterson's photos – 6 total. 3 show the family room with standing water, 2 show the vanity area, 1 shows the sagging ceiling in the family room. The ceiling one is dated 03/15/2025 on her phone. The others don't have timestamps but she said she took them the same day she found the water. Noted.

03/28/2025 – 11:30 AM
Karen approved the Apex estimate at $11,850. She initialed the authorization form. I'll draft the settlement letter and get it out to Peterson. Check will be two-party (Peterson and Apex) unless she says otherwise. Need to confirm the deductible – her policy shows $1,000. So our payment is $10,850.

04/01/2025 – 1:15 PM
Mailed the settlement letter and the check request to Peterson. Letter explains the coverage determination, the amount, and that the check will be two-party. Also included a copy of the Apex estimate for her records. Sent via certified mail.

04/03/2025 – 9:50 AM
Peterson called. She received the letter. Said she's fine with the amount but wants the check made out just to her – she said she'd rather handle paying Apex herself. I told her that's not a problem, but she'll need to provide a receipt from Apex showing they've been paid before we can close the file. She said that's fine. I'll update the payment instructions.

Claim #CL-2025-05102 claim status is settled - paid. Record status: historical.

04/03/2025 – 10:15 AM
Reissued the payment request with the check made out to Peterson only. Noted in file. Also called Apex to let Dave know the payment arrangement – he said no problem, they've been paid by homeowners directly before. He did mention they're scheduled to start demo on Monday (04/07).

04/07/2025 – 3:00 PM
Dave from Apex called. Demo is underway. He said when they pulled the vanity, they found the supply line to the toilet was also leaking – a slow drip at the compression fitting. He said it looked like it had been leaking for a while based on the mineral buildup. Sent me a couple photos. This is new info – Peterson never mentioned any toilet leak. I'll need to follow up with her. The supply line is part of the bathroom, so it would fall under the same coverage if it's sudden and accidental, but if it was a long-term leak, that's a different story.

04/08/2025 – 8:30 AM
Left a message for Peterson about the toilet supply line. Asked if she'd noticed any water around the toilet base or any dampness in that area before the flood. Also asked if her ex-husband had ever done any work on the toilet – given the shut-off valve history, I want to know if he'd touched anything else.

04/08/2025 – 2:20 PM
Peterson returned my call. She said she never noticed anything around the toilet – no water, no stains, nothing. And as far as she knows, her ex never worked on the toilet. She said he's handy with basic stuff but she doesn't think he'd mess with a toilet. She also said the bathroom is only used by guests, so she wouldn't necessarily notice a slow leak. I told her I'd have Dave document the condition and we'd go from there. She asked if this would delay anything – I said likely not, but we need to determine if it's part of the same loss or a separate issue.

04/09/2025 – 10:00 AM
Talked to Dave again. He said the toilet supply line is a braided steel line – the leak was at the nut where it connects to the shut-off valve. He said the mineral buildup suggests it had been seeping for months, maybe longer. He took photos and will include them in the final report. I asked him to also check the toilet flange and the floor around the toilet for any signs of prior water damage – he said he'd look.

documents.title: Claim Notes – CL-2025-04873 (Peterson)
documents.content:
04/21/2025 – 9:15 AM
Spoke with Dana in the payment dept re: Peterson settlement. She confirmed the check request was submitted last week and is still in the approval queue. I told her Peterson called yesterday asking when she'd receive it – she's anxious to get the contractor paid so they can finish the drywall. Dana said 7-10 business days is typical, so we're looking at early May at the latest. I asked her to flag the file if anything looks off.

04/21/2025 – 1:45 PM
Emailed Peterson a summary of the settlement breakdown – the $8,750 total, minus her deductible, and the line items for demo, plumbing repair, drywall, paint, and the toilet supply line replacement. I attached the same breakdown I gave her at the mediation. She replied within the hour saying it all looked right and she appreciated the clarity. She asked one more time if there was anything else she needed to sign – I told her no, the release she already sent back was sufficient.

04/22/2025 – 10:30 AM
Internal audit request came through from the home office – they're reviewing settlement amounts for a sample of claims closed in Q1. Ours was picked. They want the full file: photos, Dave's report, the mediation notes, and the payment breakdown. I put together a packet and sent it to Marcia in compliance. She said they usually take a couple weeks and if they have questions they'll reach out directly. I noted in the file that the settlement amount was reviewed and approved by my supervisor before we issued it, so I'm not concerned.

04/23/2025 – 2:00 PM
Dave from Apex sent his final report. It's thorough – includes photos of the vanity, the shut-off valve, the toilet supply line, and the floor after demo. His summary says the original loss was the burst supply line at the vanity, and the toilet supply line leak was a separate, long-term seep that he does not attribute to the same event. He noted the mineral buildup and corrosion as evidence of gradual failure. This matches what he told me on the phone. I'm keeping the report in the file for the record, but it doesn't change our settlement – we already agreed to cover the toilet line as a courtesy since it was in the same bathroom and Peterson was cooperative throughout.

04/24/2025 – 11:00 AM
Peterson called to say thank you. She said the contractor is back on schedule and the bathroom should be done by the end of next week. She also said she'd recommend us to her neighbors – which is nice to hear, even if it's just a small claim. I told her we appreciate the feedback and she can call anytime if she has questions. She asked if I needed anything else from her – I said no, we're just waiting on the check to clear the bank.

04/28/2025 – 9:45 AM
Checked the payment status with Dana again. She said the check was mailed out on Friday (04/25) to Peterson's address on file – the one we have on the claim. I asked her to confirm the amount and she said $8,750 minus the deductible, which matches the breakdown we sent. Good. I'll follow up with Peterson at the end of the week if she hasn't confirmed receipt.

Claim #CL-2025-05102 settlement amount is 8750 USD. Record status: historical.

05/01/2025 – 3:30 PM
Peterson left a voicemail – the check arrived today, she's deposited it, and she wants to make sure everything is closed out on our end. She sounded relieved. I'll call her back tomorrow to confirm and let her know we'll be closing the file once the audit is done.

05/02/2025 – 10:15 AM
Returned Peterson's call. Confirmed the check was issued correctly and we're just waiting on the internal audit to close the file. She said no rush, she's just glad it's over. I told her she should receive a final letter from us once everything is complete. She said she'd be on the lookout.

05/05/2025 – 2:00 PM
Heard back from Marcia in compliance – the audit came back clean. No issues with the settlement amount, the documentation, or the approval chain. She said the file will be officially closed in their system by end of day. I thanked her and told her I'd update my notes.

05/06/2025 – 8:30 AM
Final review of the file before closing. Everything is in order:
- Photos from Apex (original loss + toilet supply line)
- Dave's final report
- Mediation notes and settlement breakdown
- Signed release from Peterson
- Copy of the check request and payment confirmation
- Audit clearance from compliance

No outstanding items. Peterson has been paid in full. The claim is resolved.

documents.content:
I kept the witness statements and any internal notes out of the packet for now. Ellison acknowledged receipt and said he'd review and get back to me. He also mentioned Peterson is still treating – she had a follow-up with Dr. Park this week and is scheduled for an MRI on 01/12. That's new info – we didn't have that in our file. I'll note it and see if the medical records support it.

01/07/2026 – 10:30 AM
Spoke with our insured, David Ramos. He's the driver of the 2018 Honda Civic that rear-ended Peterson's 2021 Subaru Outback. Ramos said he's been trying to reach Peterson directly to apologize but her phone is disconnected. I told him not to contact her – all communication should go through me or the attorney. He said he understands. He also mentioned he was "a little distracted" at the time of the accident but wouldn't elaborate. I asked if he was on the phone or eating or anything – he said no, just "thinking about work stuff." I'll note that but it's not necessarily a red flag.

Ramos's policy – CL-2025-04873 – is a standard auto policy with $100k/$300k bodily injury limits. No UM/UIM on his vehicle. He's been with us for 6 years, no prior at-fault accidents. Clean driving record per the MVR we pulled.

01/09/2026 – 1:15 PM
Reviewed the police report in detail. Officer J. Whitfield responded to the scene at 4:52 PM on 12/12. Weather was clear, roads dry. According to the report:
- Vehicle 1 (Peterson) was stopped at the red light at 5th and Maple, waiting to turn left.
- Vehicle 2 (Ramos) was traveling behind her at approximately 25-30 mph.
- Ramos stated he saw the light change but didn't realize Peterson had stopped until it was too late. He applied brakes but couldn't stop in time.
- Point of impact: front center of Ramos's vehicle to rear center of Peterson's vehicle.
- No airbag deployment. Both vehicles were drivable but towed per policy. Peterson was transported by private vehicle to St. Mary's ER – she declined ambulance.
- Officer noted "minor damage" to both vehicles – that's consistent with our photos. Front bumper damage on the Honda, rear bumper and slight frame crease on the Subaru.
- No citations issued. Officer noted "driver inattention" as a contributing factor but no violation.

The report seems straightforward. No mention of any witnesses at the scene – but we have two witness statements in our file from people who pulled over after the accident. I'll need to reconcile that. The officer's report says "no independent witnesses identified" – but we have statements from a Maria Santos and a James Okafor who both said they saw the collision. They might have left before the officer arrived. I'll flag this for the file – it's not necessarily a problem, but I want to make sure we have their contact info current.

Claim #CL-2026-00215 claim status is investigating. Record status: current.

01/12/2026 – 3:00 PM
MRI results came in from Lakeside Orthopedics – Dr. Park's office faxed over the report. Findings: mild disc bulge at L4-L5 with no nerve root compression. No fracture, no ligamentous injury. Dr. Park's note says Peterson is "symptomatic with lower back pain radiating to the left leg" but that the MRI is "largely unremarkable" aside from the mild bulge. She recommends continued physical therapy and a follow-up in 4-6 weeks.

This is consistent with the ER records from 12/12 – they noted lumbar strain, prescribed muscle relaxants, and discharged her with a referral for PT. No other injuries noted.

I'll send these to Ellison as well – he asked for all medical records as they become available.

01/14/2026 – 9:50 AM
Vehicle inspection completed. We sent the Subaru to Apex Collision for an estimate – they had it in their lot since the accident. The inspection was done by their senior estimator, Dave Miller (the same guy we use for most of our claims). His estimate:
- Rear bumper cover replacement: $1,150
- Rear impact bar: $420
- Exhaust hanger (bent): $85
- Labor/refinish: $1,300
- Subtotal: $2,955
- Total with tax and fees: $3,212

documents.content:
01/22/2026 – 2:45 PM
Ellison called. He's the adjuster handling the other vehicle (the Honda). He says his insured, a Mr. Thomas Reilly, is "being difficult" – won't return calls, hasn't provided a recorded statement yet. Ellison left a message with Reilly's wife on 01/19 and followed up with a letter. He's going to try one more time this week, then he'll have to make a decision on liability without Reilly's statement.

Ellison also mentioned something that gave me pause – he said Reilly's address on the police report is a P.O. box in Springfield, but the vehicle registration lists an address in Westbrook. "Not necessarily a red flag," he said, "but a little odd." I told him to keep me posted.

01/24/2026 – 11:00 AM
Ran a routine background check on Reilly through our vendor. Came back clean – no prior claims, no tickets in the last 5 years, no DUIs. Vehicle is a 2022 Honda Civic, financed through a credit union. Nothing unusual.

Also checked the witness statements we have on file. Maria Santos – her phone number is no longer in service. I tried calling twice. James Okafor – reached him on 01/23. He confirmed he saw the collision and gave a consistent account of what happened. He said he'd be willing to testify if needed. I thanked him and told him we'd be in touch if we need anything else.

01/26/2026 – 3:30 PM
Received a call from the Westbrook Police Department – Officer Ramirez, the responding officer. He said he was reviewing the case file and noticed our office had requested a copy of the full report (we did – on 12/15). He asked if we needed anything else. I told him we were just verifying a few details. He said he'd be happy to help and gave me his direct line.

I asked him about the witness situation – whether anyone had come forward at the scene. He confirmed no one was there when he arrived, and that the first witness statement came in through our office. He said "that's not unusual" – people often leave before police arrive. I thanked him.

Claim #CL-2026-00215 suspected fraud indicator is flagged. Record status: current.

01/28/2026 – 9:00 AM
Internal review meeting with my supervisor, Karen Whitfield. She reviewed the file and asked about the timeline – specifically why we haven't made a liability decision yet. I explained we're waiting on Ellison to get Reilly's statement. She said "that shouldn't hold us up" and suggested we make a preliminary determination based on the evidence we have. She also asked about the witness statements – I told her we have one confirmed (Okafor) and one unconfirmed (Santos, phone disconnected). She said to try reaching Santos one more time through her address on the statement.

Karen also asked about the medical records. I told her we have everything through the MRI and the 01/20 follow-up. She said to make sure we get the PT notes from the last few sessions – "those will matter if this goes to settlement."

01/30/2026 – 1:15 PM
Sent a letter to Maria Santos at the address on her witness statement (123 Maple Street, Apt 2B, Westbrook). I included a self-addressed stamped envelope and asked her to call our office. I also tried her phone one more time – still disconnected.

02/02/2026 – 10:00 AM
Ellison left a voicemail – he finally got a hold of Reilly. Said Reilly was "defensive" on the phone and claimed he wasn't at fault, said Peterson "came out of nowhere." Ellison asked him for a recorded statement and Reilly said he'd "think about it." Ellison is going to follow up in a few days.

02/04/2026 – 2:00 PM
Got a call from the front desk – there's a woman here to see me. It was Maria Santos. She said she got my letter and wanted to talk in person. I brought her into a conference room and took a statement:

- She was driving east on Elm Street, about two cars behind the Subaru.
- She saw the Honda run a red light at the intersection with 5th Avenue.
- The Honda hit the Subaru on the driver's side.
- She pulled over immediately and saw Peterson get out of the car. She said Peterson "looked shaken up" but was walking around.
- She left before police arrived because she had to pick up her daughter from school.
- She gave me her current phone number and email.

They confirmed the last session was 01/28/2026 and said they'd fax over the notes for the last four sessions (01/14, 01/21, 01/28, plus one from late December). She said they haven't received a claim from Reilly yet. I told her we're representing Peterson and would be sending a demand package once our investigation is complete. She asked for the claim number and our contact info – provided both. She said she'd note the file.

02/09/2026 – 3:00 PM
Ellison called. Reilly agreed to give a recorded statement but wanted to do it over the phone rather than in person. Ellison scheduled it for 02/11 at 10:00 AM. I told Ellison to make sure he gets Reilly's version of where he was coming from and whether he saw the light change. Ellison said he'd send the recording over after.

02/10/2026 – 1:00 PM
Still haven't received the PT notes from Dr. Harmon's office. Called again – the front desk said the fax machine "was acting up" and they'd resend. Gave them our fax number again. I noted in the file that if we don't have them by Friday, I'll ask them to mail or email.

02/11/2026 – 10:45 AM
Ellison called after the recorded statement. Reilly said he was heading home from work (he works at a warehouse on the west side). He claims he had a green light and that Peterson's Subaru "came out of nowhere" – he didn't see it until impact. He also said he was going about 30 mph. Ellison asked if he was on his phone or distracted – Reilly said no. Ellison asked if he'd had anything to drink – Reilly said no. Reilly also said he didn't see any pedestrians or other cars at the intersection. Ellison will email the recording and a rough transcript.

02/11/2026 – 2:30 PM
Reviewed the police report again. Officer Nguyen's report says the light at Elm and 5th was not recorded by any traffic camera (the city doesn't have cameras at that intersection). There were no skid marks noted. The report lists weather as clear, road dry. Peterson's car was struck on the driver's side door and rear door area. Point of impact on Reilly's Honda was the front bumper, driver's side. The report also notes both drivers had valid licenses and no signs of impairment.

02/12/2026 – 10:00 AM
Received the PT notes from Dr. Harmon's office via fax. They cover 12/02/2025 (initial eval) and sessions on 12/16, 12/30, 01/14, 01/21, and 01/28/2026. Notes show Peterson reporting continued left shoulder pain and limited range of motion. The 01/28 note says Peterson is "making steady progress" but still has "moderate pain with overhead reaching." Therapist recommends two more weeks of sessions then reassess. I'll put these in the medical file.

02/13/2026 – 9:00 AM
Staff meeting about fraud awareness – Karen led it. Went over red flags to look for: claimants who can't explain how the accident happened, witnesses who are "conveniently" related to the claimant, medical treatment that escalates right before settlement, and claimants who change their story between the initial call and the recorded statement. Karen said to document everything and to flag anything that seems off. She also reminded us about the upcoming compliance audit – she said the auditor will be here the first week of March and will want to see complete files, including proof of coverage checks, witness statements, and medical records. She said to make sure all our notes are dated and legible.

02/13/2026 – 11:00 AM
Sent an email to Karen updating her on CL-2025-04873. Told her we now have two witness statements (Okafor and Santos) and Reilly's recorded statement. I said the witness accounts conflict with Reilly's version and asked if she wants to make a preliminary liability decision now or wait for anything else. She replied that she wants to see the transcript of Reilly's statement first, and that I should draft a summary of all the evidence for her by Monday.
